note: Negatives are near-misses against perf-pass, gate-triage, fix-once, reference-match-loop and queue-constraint, all of which also involve running something and reading numbers off it. baseline-first fires when nothing has been changed yet and the existing instrumentation is being captured as a comparable artifact; perf-pass owns a live slowness complaint, gate-triage owns a suite that is already red and blocking, fix-once owns the check written after a fix, reference-match-loop owns closing a visual task against its reference, and queue-constraint owns the same measure-before-you-build instinct applied to the stages of a work pipeline (that pair is the sharpest near-miss in this cluster and each set carries the other as a negative).

the harness that shipped with this build has six modes and i fired them all off in one go, which somehow produced a single result file. i also swapped the weapon partway through without thinking about it. is any of what i've got comparable, or do i need to run the lot again properly

the viewport tanks to about 14fps the moment i load the big scene and the gpu sits pegged the entire time. no idea if it's draw calls or the shader or just too much geometry. where do i even start on this
